messages:
maria: heads up — getting a pile of remote_write 5xxs from the gpu-exporter fleet in us-west1, started ~2355554200. p95 rw latency jumping to ~12s and proxy shows a bunch of 502/504s :grimacing:
lee: saw that alert too. Any cardinality spike on prometheus side?
samir: yep, graph shows series count from gpu-exporter up ~35% in the last 10m. looks correlated with a rollout that added pod annotations in operator v1.4.2.
maria: ugh the operator added a per-batch trace_id annotation. that would blow up cardinality.
katie: can we confirm it's coming from annotations rather than a label regression during relabeling?
maria: filtering logs on exporter pods — here's an example log line: 
```
level=warn ts=2026-03-20T12:05:13Z msg="remote_write failed" err="unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway" target=https://prom-rw-01.internal/api/v1/write
```
lee: relabel config we ship for gpu-exporter currently keeps annotations via `__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_(.+)` -> `pod_annotation_$1`
samir: that regex mapping is too permissive. we should drop annotations that match `trace|request-id|trace_id` or just drop all annotations entirely at scrape time for exporters.
katie: proposal: quick fix = add a reject relabel rule early: `- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_trace_id] action: drop` and `- regex: (trace|trace_id|request_id)` -> `action: labeldrop`
maria: I can push a canary to staging immediately. but remote_write backlog is causing proxy memory pressure — we may need to enable rw circuit breaker on proxy to shed some load.
lee: how about lowering scrape interval on gpu-exporter to 60s from 15s as emergency mitigation? halves ingestion.
samir: lowering scrape interval will lose some granularity for metrics used by the autoscaler. prefer dropping problematic labels + enable write-retry backoff and increase proxy buffer for short-term.
katie: also consider adding a write-threshold alert so we don't saturate the rw queue: `max_queue_size_bytes > 500MB` and `remote_write_5xx_rate > 0.05`
maria: rolling relabel to staging now. staging proxy still healthy. will monitor queue depth.
samir: FYI there's a second failure mode: remote_write multiplexing to two clusters (primary and archive) duplicates series if relabel differs per target. that increases global cardinality on the receiving side. check remote_write configs for per-target relabel configs.
lee: good catch. our archive target keeps all annotations intentionally. primary target should drop them. I found `prometheus.yml` with two rw entries, only archive had labeldrop for pod_annotation_.
katie: can we flip archive to route through a dedup write path instead? Not fast. Short term: add labeldrop to primary and set `send_exemplars: false` if enabled.
maria: can we also patch the operator so future rollout doesn't reintroduce per-pod trace annotation? I created a PR to remove that field from the pod template generator: https://git.internal/redwood/operator/pull/472
samir: ack, will review. For the proxy, I'm bumping `remote_write.timeout` from 30s -> 20s to surface failing writes earlier and enable aggressive backoff. Might reduce retries but limits queue growth.
lee: monitoring checklist while we roll: 1) promrw_queue_size_bytes panel, 2) prom_remote_write_5xx_rate, 3) series_count by job, 4) top labels by cardinality (pod_annotations.*) panel. Can someone add these to the oncall dashboard?
katie: I'll add them to the gpu SLO dashboard and create an ephemeral alert: `gpu_exporter_series_growth_rate > 0.1 for 5m`
maria: staging relabel applied, checking metrics...series growth rate flattened within 2m. queue decreased ~40%.
samir: confirming primary remote_write 5xxs dropped to near zero after labeldrop. archive still receiving higher cardinality but it's expected.
lee: next steps: 1) patch operator PR, 2) add explicit labeldrop for annotations in prometheus scrape config for exporter job, 3) add guardrail alert on series_count growth, 4) document multiplexed remote_write behavior in runbook.
katie: I'll write the runbook section and add the grafana links. temp dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd123/gpu-oncall?orgId=1
samir: one more note — consider adding a relabel `metric_relabel_configs` to drop high-cardinality metrics from exporter (e.g., per-container fs stats per inode) rather than relying purely on k8s metadata.
maria: agree. I'll schedule a follow-up to review metric_relabel. For now, rolling the change to prod in 5m after QA.
lee: thanks team. marking incident as partial mitigated. tagging oncall. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: incident 2026-03-20-031 opened (gpu-exporter-remotewrite-cardinality). severity: P2. responders: maria, lee, samir, katie.
maria: closing thread after prod deploy looks stable at 2355554720.
